newsitem.title: USA: DC mayor urges senator to step down from DC panel.
newsitem.headline: DC mayor urges senator to step down from DC panel.

text.p: District of Columbia Mayor Marion Barry on Tuesday said the chairman of a key U.S. House panel should step down because of his "lack of respect" for D.C. leaders.

Barry said that Sen. Lauch Faircloth, R-N.C., should resign as head of the Senate Appropriations Committee's subpanel on D.C. because Faircloth did not invite D.C. officials to participate in a March 11 hearing affecting the city.

Faircloth and chairmen of three other House and Senate panels that oversee D.C. finances heard testimony from mayors of several U.S. cities that have overcome or avoided financial emergencies, including Philadelphia; Indianapolis; Charlotte, N.C.; and San Diego.

"Senator Faircloth should either be replaced as Chairman or resign. Enough is enough," Barry said. "He has consistently shown narrow-mindedness, shortsightedness, personal bias and sheer contempt for the District and its residents," Barry said. "It is ridiculous and it must stop."
A spokesman for Faircloth said, "Marion Barry and his press secretary are playing reelection politics way too soon."
The spokesman said the hearing was not chaired by Faircloth, but by Rep. Charles Taylor, R-N.C., chairman of the House Appropriations Committee subpanel on D.C.
"There will be other hearings with local elected and appointed officials," he added.
